linkNotes.aaron|christ-high-priest: Worthington: Aaron, with Moses, a figure of Christ — the high priest prefiguring Christ the High Priest.
linkNotes.absalom|unbelievers-rejection-of-christ-: Worthington: David's people revolting (under Absalom and Seba) while he had subdued the nations prefigured the chosen people rejecting Christ while the Gentiles were converted: 'The reprobation of the former was prefigured by those rebels.'
linkNotes.ahithophel|the-betrayal-by-judas: Bible de Vence: Christ applies to Judas what David said of Achitophel, 'who was thus a figure of the perfidious Judas.'
linkNotes.antiochus-epiphanes|antichrist: Challoner: the little horn 'may also be applied to that great persecutor, Antiochus Epiphanes, as a figure of antichrist.'
linkNotes.babylon|babylon-the-great-the-harlot: Calmet/Witham: 'it was the great Babylon, as St. Peter... calls it' (1 Pet 5:13); the harlot signifies Rome and all the wicked.
linkNotes.binding-of-isaac|christs-passion: On Gen 22:14: 'Jehovah will provide a victim, even Jesus Christ in the same place' — the victim provided at Moriah figures Christ the sacrifice.
linkNotes.binding-of-isaac|the-resurrection: Challoner: Abraham received Isaac back 'in a parable... as a figure of Christ slain and coming to life again.'
linkNotes.brazen-serpent|christs-passion: Christ himself (John 3:14): the brazen serpent lifted up in the desert (Num 21) 'is a figure of the crucifixion of Christ on Calvary.'
linkNotes.ceremonial-law|the-gospel-new-covenant: Witham: the Jewish festivals, new moons, and sabbaths were 'shadows, types and figures' fulfilled in the new law of Christ.
linkNotes.ceremonial-law|the-one-true-church: Worthington: 'the mysteries of the Church, prefigured by the Jewish rites.'
linkNotes.circumcision|baptism: Circumcision prefigures that 'circumcision of Christ' which is Baptism
linkNotes.cloud-in-desert|baptism: The cloud that led Israel prefigured Baptism
linkNotes.cyrus|christ: Calmet: 'Cyrus was a figure of the Messias.'
linkNotes.daniels-four-beasts-four-empires|antichr: Pastorini/Haydock: the beast 'composed of the territories of the three preceding empires, which are represented by Daniel under the figure of these animals.'
linkNotes.david|the-betrayal-by-judas: Christ himself applies the verse to Judas (John 13:18): 'he that eateth bread with me, shall lift up his heel against me.'
linkNotes.david|the-one-true-church: Jerome/Augustine: the psalm is explained 'of the victories of David, of the Messias, and of his Church' — David figures the just in the Church.
linkNotes.david|the-resurrection: St. Jerome: 'I shall be filled, when I shall awake in thy likeness' read of the resurrection (Phil 3:21; 1 Cor 13:12) — David's awakening prefigures the resurrection of the just.
linkNotes.deborah|mary: CCC 489: "Throughout the Old Covenant the mission of many holy women prepared for that of Mary" (naming Eve, Sarah, Hannah, Deborah, Ruth, Judith and Esther).
linkNotes.deborah|the-one-true-church: Haydock/Worthington: Debora's victory over Sisara (with Jael) figures the Church's spiritual conquests — 'soon after the preaching of the gospel, the most potent monarchs submitted to its authority.'
linkNotes.destruction-of-jerusalem-as-divine-judgm: Worthington: the ruin of Jerusalem by Titus 'is a figure of the world's destruction, and of the eternal punishment of the wicked.'
linkNotes.dietary-laws|the-gospel-new-covenant: Witham: the distinction of clean/unclean meats were 'shadows, types and figures of future things to be fulfilled in the new law of Christ; but the body is of Christ.'
linkNotes.divine-fire-lightning|descent-of-the-hol: Worthington: 'The Holy Ghost appeared in the form of parted tongues of fire, to enable the apostles to convert' the world (Acts 2:3).
linkNotes.edom|persecutors-of-the-church: Challoner: 'Edom and Bosra... are here taken in a mystical sense for the enemies of Christ and his Church.'
linkNotes.elijah|john-the-baptist: Calmet: 'Our Saviour testifies that the Elias whom the Jews expected was already come' (Matt 11:14).
linkNotes.esau|the-reprobate-the-rejected: St. Augustine: Esau 'was a figure of the reprobate, though not of course one himself.'
linkNotes.esther|mary: St. Thomas Aquinas: 'Esther was also a type of the blessed Virgin, by whose intercession the head of the serpent is crushed.'
linkNotes.esther|the-one-true-church: St. Jerome: Esther 'is given as a pattern of Christian sovereigns, and a figure of the Church.'
linkNotes.eve|mary: CCC 489: "Throughout the Old Covenant the mission of many holy women prepared for that of Mary" (naming Eve, Sarah, Hannah, Deborah, Ruth, Judith and Esther).
linkNotes.gods-deliverance-from-sennacherib|final-: Worthington: persecutors 'will all be terrified when the signs of judgment begin to appear in heaven, which are here represented as past, on account of their certainty.'
linkNotes.gods-healing-word|christ: St. Athanasius (Fathers): 'Word. Jesus Christ, according to the prophetical sense' (cf. Matt 8:7).
linkNotes.gods-wonders-by-water|baptism: Worthington: 'God has wrought many wonders by water... to prefigure the graces conferred in baptism.'
linkNotes.gog-and-magog|final-judgment: St. Augustine: 'this will be the last persecution at the approach of the day of judgment, which the whole Church... will suffer' — Gog and Magog dispersed through the nations.
linkNotes.hannah|mary: CCC 489: "Throughout the Old Covenant the mission of many holy women prepared for that of Mary" (naming Eve, Sarah, Hannah, Deborah, Ruth, Judith and Esther).
linkNotes.hezekiah|christ: St. Jerome/Calmet: 'This regards Christ, prefigured by Ezechias.'
linkNotes.hezekiah|the-one-true-church: Calmet: 'Was not his reign a figure of the Church persecuted and increasing...?'
linkNotes.holofernes|antichrist: Worthington: 'He is a figure of Antichrist; for whom all heretics pave the way' (2 Thess 2).
linkNotes.hosea|christ: Calmet: 'He acts as a figure of the Lord, who has received an outrage'; grace is still offered to sinners.
linkNotes.isaac|the-gospel-new-covenant: Witham: 'by Isaac is represented the new covenant or testament of Christ.'
linkNotes.isaac|the-one-true-church: Witham: Christians 'shall be accounted the spiritual children of Abraham,' heirs as Isaac was.
linkNotes.isaiah-the-prophet|christ: Calmet: 'Isaias may here speak of himself, yet only as a figure of Christ'; the Jews admit the Messias is meant.
linkNotes.ishmael|heretics: St. Augustine: Ishmael/Hagar are 'a figure of heretics (who are the children of the bond-woman) unjustly persecuting the Catholic Church.'
linkNotes.ishmael|the-mosaic-law: Paul's allegory (Witham): Ismael, born of the bond-woman, 'represent[s] that covenant of the former law delivered on Mount Sina' — bondage and fear.
linkNotes.israel-jeshurun|christ: Berthier: 'Jeshurun is a title of Israel... who was a figure of the Messias, the beloved of God.'
linkNotes.israel-jeshurun|the-one-true-church: Witham: 'the Israelites of the Christians' — Israel delivered through the Red Sea, singing, figures the Christians who have passed through persecution.
linkNotes.israels-disobedience-in-the-wilderness|f: 'this was done and written to teach us'; baptism and communion 'will prove our greater condemnation' if our life does not correspond (1 Cor 10:6,11).
linkNotes.jacob|the-elect-predestinate: St. Augustine: 'Jacob was a figure of the elect or predestinate,' favored purely by God's mercy.
linkNotes.jeremiah|christs-passion: St. Jerome: 'all the prophets did most things for a type of our Lord... what was now done by Jeremias, foreshewed what would happen to our Lord.'
linkNotes.job|christ: St. Gregory/Worthington: 'we may consider him as a lively figure of Christ; who was perfectly innocent, and yet a man of sorrows' (Heb 4:15; 13:12).
linkNotes.job|christs-passion: Menochius/Worthington: 'Job was herein a figure of Christ' — his being spat upon and held in contempt prefigures Christ's passion (Matt 26).
linkNotes.job|the-one-true-church: St. Gregory (via Worthington): Job 'was a figure of the Church, defending the common cause; while his friends, like heretics, speak both true and false things.'
linkNotes.job|the-resurrection: Calmet: Job's anticipated restoration is 'an earnest and figure of the resurrection'; St. Paul: 'If Christ be risen, we also shall rise again.'
linkNotes.jonah|christs-passion: Calmet: 'He was cast into the sea to save those on board; Christ dies for the redemption of mankind.'
linkNotes.jonah|the-gentiles-grafted-into-christs-: Calmet: Jonah preached only after his deliverance; 'thus the gospel was designed to be preached to the Gentiles, yet Christ would not have it done till he had risen.'
linkNotes.jonah|the-resurrection: Worthington/Augustine: 'The resurrection, prefigured by Jonas, was the great proof of Christ and his Church.'
linkNotes.jordan-crossing|baptism: Baptism is prefigured in the crossing of the Jordan River
linkNotes.jordan-crossing|eternal-life: Entry into the Promised Land is an image of eternal life
linkNotes.josedec|christ-high-priest: Calmet: 'He was a noble figure of Christ, and helped to build the temple' (Zech 3:1; 6:11).
linkNotes.josias|final-judgment: St. Jerome/Worthington: 'The lamentation for Josias, represents that of impenitent sinners at the day of judgment.'
linkNotes.judas-maccabeus|christ: Calmet: 'Judas was also a figure of Christ, the chief corner-stone, and he should be born of that tribe [Judah].'
linkNotes.judas-maccabeus|christs-passion: Calmet: Judas, greatly bewailed (1 Macc 9:20), 'was a figure of Christ, whom the prophet had chiefly in view' — the pierced and mourned one.
linkNotes.judas-maccabeus|christs-victory: Calmet/St. Dionysius: 'Judas, the Machabee, the glorious figure of Christ'; the first six verses applied to the Saviour's ascension after victory.
linkNotes.judith|mary: Fulbert/Worthington: 'Judith was a figure of the blessed Virgin, to whom these praises chiefly belong.'
linkNotes.judith|the-one-true-church: Calmet: 'contemplate in her a glorious figure of the Christian Church, which is spotless... overcomes the power of persecutors, giving all the glory to God.'
linkNotes.leviathan|satan-the-devil: Worthington: 'This huge fish, perhaps the whale, representing the devil, is subject to God.' Category Eschatological (the devil's subjection/defeat); could be read Christologically.
linkNotes.levitical-leprosy-laws|christ: Ven. Bede: 'By this leper is represented the whole human race, which was covered with a spiritual leprosy' — cleansed by Christ who took our nature.
linkNotes.levitical-purifications-ceremonial-washi: Worthington: 'the purification of the Jews... prefigured baptism and penance' (Eph 5:26; Titus 3:5).
linkNotes.liver-of-the-fish-tobit|christs-passion: St. Augustine/Prosper/Worthington: 'This mystically represented the Passion of Christ, by which the devil is expelled from men's hearts.' Confidence medium: allegorical/mystical reading.
linkNotes.manna|christ: St. Augustine: the manna 'was only a figure of himself [Christ], who came down from heaven to give life to the world' — the true Bread of Life.
linkNotes.manna|eucharist: Manna in the desert prefigured the Eucharist, the true bread from heaven
linkNotes.melchizedek|christ-high-priest: Melchizedek is a prefiguration of the priesthood of Christ
linkNotes.melchizedek|eucharist: Melchizedek's offering of bread and wine prefigures the Eucharist
linkNotes.mosess-veil|the-gospel-new-covenant: Estius: St. Paul gives 'the allegorical explanation of the light and veil on the face of Moses' — the apostles speak without a veil under the New Covenant.
linkNotes.nehemiah|christ: Ven. Bede/Worthington/Haydock: Nehemiah's name and mission prefigured Christ sent to comfort and establish his Church.
linkNotes.noahs-ark|baptism: The ark that saved through water prefigures baptismal salvation
linkNotes.noahs-flood|baptism: The flood and Noah's ark prefigured salvation by Baptism
linkNotes.ot-priesthood|christ-high-priest: Everything that the priesthood of the Old Covenant prefigured finds fulfillment in Christ
linkNotes.ot-sacrifices|eucharist: The daily sacrifice 'taken away' (Dan 12:11) 'is understood of the sacrifice of the mass, which Antichrist will endeavour to suppress.'
linkNotes.ot-sacrifices|new-covenant-sacraments: The Church sees in OT liturgical signs a prefiguring of the sacraments of the New Covenant
linkNotes.ot-sacrifices|the-gospel-new-covenant: Witham: the first testament, ratified by the blood of victims, was 'only a figure of the second or new testament,' confirmed by the death of Christ.
linkNotes.passover|christs-passion: The paschal lamb, whose bones were not broken, prefigures Christ crucified with unbroken bones (John 19:36).
linkNotes.passover|eucharist: Jesus gave new and definitive meaning to the Passover blessing of bread and cup
linkNotes.proselytes-strangers-in-israel|the-genti: Commentary explicit: 'These strangers prefigured the Gentiles, chosen to build the Christian Church.'
linkNotes.proselytes-strangers-in-israel|the-one-t: Calmet: Jerusalem 'received strangers within her walls, as a figure of the Christian Church' (Isa 2:2; Zech 8:20).
linkNotes.raphael|christ: Ven. Bede/Worthington: 'This angel prefigured Jesus Christ, who took indeed our human nature.' Confidence medium: the analogy is imperfect (Raphael only appeared in human form).
linkNotes.red-sea-crossing|baptism: The cloud and the crossing of the Red Sea prefigured Baptism
linkNotes.red-sea-crossing|christs-victory: The crossing of the Red Sea is a sign or type of Christ's victory
linkNotes.red-sea-crossing|the-saints-in-heavenly-: Calmet: the Red Sea Moses passed, 'so similar to the deliverance of the saints from the persecutions,' who sing the canticle of Moses in heaven.
linkNotes.return-from-babylonian-captivity|christ: Calmet: Christ, 'whose redemption was prefigured by the former event' (the return from captivity); St. Paul applies vv.26-28 to Christ.
linkNotes.return-from-babylonian-captivity|christs: 'Christ, by dying, conquered death... This was faintly represented by the liberation of the captives' (1 Cor 15:54).
linkNotes.return-from-babylonian-captivity|the-con: Calmet: St. Paul proves the Jews will at last be converted (Rom 11:26); 'The return of the captives prefigured this event.'
linkNotes.return-from-babylonian-captivity|the-gen: 'under the figure of the deliverance from captivity, [Isaiah] points out the vocation of the Gentiles' (Luke 7:22).
linkNotes.return-from-babylonian-captivity|the-one: Haydock: the prophets describe those returning from captivity as holy people, 'a figure of the Church.'
linkNotes.return-from-babylonian-captivity|the-res: Calmet: the prophet's promise of 'a sort of resurrection' was 'a figure of the real sufferings and rising of Jesus Christ'; St. Paul applies it (1 Cor 15:55).
linkNotes.ruth|mary: CCC 489: "Throughout the Old Covenant the mission of many holy women prepared for that of Mary" (naming Eve, Sarah, Hannah, Deborah, Ruth, Judith and Esther).
linkNotes.samson|the-resurrection: St. Gregory: Samson, 'a figure of Christ,' arose at midnight and carried away the gates of Gaza — figuring Christ's resurrection breaking the gates of death.
linkNotes.sanaballat|heretics: Ven. Bede/Worthington: Sanaballat 'was a persecutor, and prefigured heretics.'
linkNotes.sarah|mary: CCC 489: "Throughout the Old Covenant the mission of many holy women prepared for that of Mary" (naming Eve, Sarah, Hannah, Deborah, Ruth, Judith and Esther).
linkNotes.sennacherib|persecutors-of-the-church: Calmet: 'He was a figure of persecutors of the Church, to which many passages here allude.'
linkNotes.solomon|christ: Worthington: 'Herein Solomon was a figure of Christ, who is styled the Prince of peace' (Isa 9).
linkNotes.solomon|christ-church: Calmet: passages of Ps 44(45) refer to Solomon's marriage to Pharaoh's daughter 'as a figure of Christ's union with his Church.'
linkNotes.temporal-chastisements-of-israel|final-j: Berthier/Grotius: 'Temporal chastisements were intended to prefigure those which are eternal' (Matt 19; 1 Cor 10:8).
linkNotes.temporal-rewards-of-the-old-law|eternal-: Worthington: 'God gave temporal advantages to the just in the old law, as a figure of heavenly rewards.'
linkNotes.the-abomination-of-desolation|antichrist: Witham: the abomination 'will be more completely fulfilled by Antichrist and his precursors' (Dan 9; Matt 24).
linkNotes.the-altar-of-incense|christ: Witham: 'The altar seems to signify our Saviour Christ, as the prayers of all the faithful are always made through the merits of Christ, our only chief Mediator.'
linkNotes.the-altar-of-incense|the-saints-in-heave: Witham: 'The incense from the censer is said to be the prayers of all the Saints, which the Angel offered up.'
linkNotes.the-angel-of-the-lord|christ: Calmet: 'This is explained of Jesus Christ, by St. Augustine and St. Jerome.'
linkNotes.the-ark-of-the-covenant|christ: St. Ambrose/Calmet: 'these promises refer to the Messias, prefigured by the ark'; God raised minds from sensible things to Christ.
linkNotes.the-ark-of-the-covenant|heaven: Haydock: 'David always desired to be near the ark... as the figure of heaven.'
linkNotes.the-ark-of-the-covenant|mary: CCC 2676: Mary "is the daughter of Zion in person, the ark of the covenant, the place where the glory of the Lord dwells."
linkNotes.the-ass-and-the-colt-palm-sunday|the-one: St. Chrysostom: 'Both Jews and Gentiles, figured by the ass and the colt, are to be loosed and conducted by the hands of the apostles of Christ to their Redeemer.'
linkNotes.the-babylonian-exile|destruction-of-jeru: Origen/St. Jerome: the exile 'was only a figure of what they endured since they rejected Christ.'
linkNotes.the-cup-of-divine-wrath|final-judgment: Worthington: the bitter chalice of the damned (fire, gall, brimstone) figures the cup of God's wrath at the final judgment (Apoc 14:10; Isa 51:17; Ezek 23:34). Imagery-based figure.
linkNotes.the-divine-chariot-theophany|christs-asc: St. Athanasius and others explain the chariot theophany of Christ's ascension.
linkNotes.the-dove-and-the-olive-branch-noah|bapti: St. Ambrose: the peace of baptism, 'prefigured by the olive branch which the dove carried back to the ark, a true figure of the Church.'
linkNotes.the-exodus-from-egypt|christ: Du Hamel: 'The redemption of man was prefigured by the liberation of the Jews.'
linkNotes.the-faithful-remnant|the-one-true-church: Calmet: 'The few who were converted under Ezechias were a figure of those who should embrace the faith of Christ.'
linkNotes.the-feast-on-mount-zion|eucharist: Calmet: Sion 'a figure of the Church, and of heaven... some of all nations shall partake of the blessed Eucharist.'
linkNotes.the-feast-on-mount-zion|heaven: Calmet: 'The expressions are too grand for a corruptible feast' — the banquet figures the heavenly consummation.
linkNotes.the-foolish-shepherd|persecutors-of-the-: Challoner: 'to represent the foolish, that is, the wicked princes and priests that should rule the people, before their utter desolation' — Caligula, Claudius, Nero.
linkNotes.the-gates-lifted-for-the-king-of-glory|c: Theodoret/Eusebius: 'The Church has constantly understood this passage of Christ's ascension'; the saints in his train address the astonished angels.
linkNotes.the-glory-of-the-lord-departing-the-temp: Theodoret/Calmet: the throne figure (upper/lower body differing, denoting the two natures) departing by Olivet represents Christ's ascension.
Calmet: the glory's departure shows 'how Jerusalem would be treated, and the Jews suffer after the ascension of our Saviour.'
linkNotes.the-golden-candlestick-menorah|christ: Calmet: the oil-fed candlestick (the Spirit) — 'The Messias would receive the fulness of this spirit' (Isa 11:2).
linkNotes.the-golden-candlestick-menorah|the-one-t: Witham: the seven golden candlesticks 'represented the seven Churches of Asia' (allusion to Exod 25:31).
linkNotes.the-heavenly-jerusalem-prophetic-vision|: Calmet: St. John (Apoc. 21:10) 'represents the church in the same ornaments, denoting the merits of Christ and the virtues of his saints.'
linkNotes.the-heavens|the-one-true-church: Berthier (the Fathers): 'Heaven denotes the Church, as the stars represent apostolic men' who labor day and night, in peace and persecution.
linkNotes.the-holy-of-holies|christs-ascension: Witham: the way into the holies 'was not to be opened till Christ, the high priest, first entered, by shedding his blood on the cross, and by his glorious ascension.'
linkNotes.the-holy-of-holies|heaven: Witham: 'the holy of holies, which was a figure of heaven, into which Christ Jesus himself entered first, by his glorious ascension.'
linkNotes.the-invitation-to-the-waters-isaiah-55|n: St. Jerome/Calmet: wine and honey were given to the newly baptized; 'Christ invites all to come to him' (John 4:14; 7:37).
linkNotes.the-king-of-tyre|satan-the-devil: Challoner: 'what is here said to him is commonly understood of Lucifer, the king over all the children of pride.'
linkNotes.the-kings-of-sheba-bearing-gifts|the-ado: Worthington: 'The three kings came on swift beasts to adore Christ, and fulfilled his prophecy, Matthew 2.'
linkNotes.the-living-waters-from-the-sanctuary|the: Challoner: 'the fountain of grace in the Church militant, and of glory in the Church triumphant.'
linkNotes.the-mark-of-tau|baptism: Worthington: 'those who shall be saved, received the mark of his cross,' the sign 'used in conferring baptism, consecrating the blessed Eucharist.'
linkNotes.the-mark-of-tau|final-judgment: Worthington: the cross 'will be borne before Christ, at his last coming (Matt 24), to the joy of those who have performed their baptismal promises, and to the confusion of the enemies of the cross.'
linkNotes.the-mincha-unbloody-sacrifice|eucharist: Worthington: the mincha is 'a sacrifice of flour, or unbloody; a figure of the Mass.'
linkNotes.the-mosaic-law|christ: Haydock: 'as the law and the prophets are fulfilled and verified in Jesus Christ, your new legislator and prophet, you are to hear and obey Him.'
linkNotes.the-mosaic-law|heaven: Witham: the law was 'but a shadow' of 'the good things to come,' which some understand of 'heaven itself, and the happiness of the elect.'
linkNotes.the-mosaic-law|the-gospel-new-covenant: 'The gospel has perfected or fulfilled the law' (Matt 5:17).
linkNotes.the-pool-of-siloam|baptism: Calmet: 'The pool of Siloe represents the sacrament of baptism, by which we are sanctified and made Christians.'
linkNotes.the-pool-of-siloam|christ: Calmet: 'The word Siloe signifies sent, and was a figure of Christ, who was sent by his eternal Father into the world to enlighten all men.'
linkNotes.the-promised-land|heaven: Haydock/Worthington: God will bring the penitent 'into the land of rectitude, which is heaven.'
linkNotes.the-prophets|christ: Calmet: 'The prophets prefigured Christ, the end of the law.'
linkNotes.the-prophets|descent-of-the-holy-spirit-: Worthington: the post-captivity prophets were 'only a shadow of what would befall true believers' — the outpouring of the Spirit (Acts 2; 1 Cor 14:24).
linkNotes.the-rebuilt-temple|christ: Worthington: 'The rebuilding of the temple is foretold, as a figure of man's redemption.'
linkNotes.the-rebuilt-temple|the-one-true-church: Calmet/Menochius: the temple's survival despite persecution figures the Church against which 'the gates of hell shall not prevail' (Matt 16:18).
linkNotes.the-rechabites|religious-orders-consecra: Worthington: 'Here we behold a figure of religious orders in the Church... they observed certain rules for acquiring greater perfection.'
linkNotes.the-rejected-cornerstone|christ: Calmet: David, Zorobabel, the nation 'can only be considered as figures of Christ, in whom this prediction was fulfilled' (Matt 21:42; Acts 4:11).
linkNotes.the-rejected-cornerstone|the-one-true-ch: 'He has laid the foundation. We must be living stones, if we would co-operate in this heavenly building' (1 Pet 2:5) — Christ the cornerstone of the Church.
linkNotes.the-scapegoat-day-of-atonement|christs-p: Witham: the sin-offering burnt outside the camp on the day of expiation — 'when he fulfilled this figure... Jesus... was pleased to suffer out of the gate of Jerusalem.'
linkNotes.the-shepherd-of-israel|christ: Witham: 'The Lamb... shall rule them as a shepherd does his flock... shall lead them unto fountains of living waters.'
linkNotes.the-son-of-isaiah-emmanuel-sign|christ: Calmet: the prophet 'speaks of Jesus Christ... as well as of a boy, who should prefigure him.'
linkNotes.the-spouse-of-the-canticle-song-of-songs: Calmet/Cassiodorus: 'The Gentile Church is eager to be guided by the one true Shepherd, and adheres to him with the greatest fervour' during persecution.
linkNotes.the-stone-daniels-vision|the-one-true-ch: Calmet: 'the kingdom of Christ gains ground, and will flourish till that of Rome shall be no more.'
linkNotes.the-sun|christ: Berthier (the Fathers): 'Jesus Christ is the true sun of justice, enlightening every man that cometh into the world' (John 1).
linkNotes.the-synagogue-old-covenant-assembly|the-: St. Augustine: 'The synagogue rejected the Messias, but God received him, and made him head of the Church.'
linkNotes.the-tabernacle-gods-dwelling-place|heave: Berthier/Worthington: 'Heaven is also styled a tabernacle and mountain... and is here chiefly meant' — the earthly sanctuary prefigures the heavenly dwelling (cf. Heb 8-9).
linkNotes.the-temple-of-jerusalem|christ: Theodoret: 'The Fathers explain it of Jesus Christ, who was born at Bethlehem, and was prefigured by the temple.'
linkNotes.the-temple-of-jerusalem|heaven: St. Augustine: the Corites 'represent the faithful upon earth, who sigh after the heavenly Sion' — earthly Zion figures the heavenly Jerusalem.
linkNotes.the-temple-of-jerusalem|the-one-true-chu: Haydock: the temple's stability and uniqueness 'was fulfilled in the Church of Jesus Christ.'
linkNotes.the-threshing-floor|final-judgment: Ven. Bede: the cleansing of the floor 'most especially at the end of the world, when the Son of man shall send his angels to gather... all scandals.'
linkNotes.the-threshing-floor|the-one-true-church: Ven. Bede: 'By the barn-floor is here prefigured the Church of Christ, in which many are called, but few are chosen.'
linkNotes.the-twelve-patriarchs|the-twelve-apostle: Menochius: Christ chose 12 apostles 'that they might correspond to the number of the Jewish patriarchs, by whom they may be said to have been prefigured.'
linkNotes.the-unbroken-bones-of-the-just|christs-p: Berthier: 'this prediction was fulfilled in his person, as St. John (19:36) does not confine himself to the type of the paschal lamb.'
linkNotes.the-vineyard-of-israel|the-gospel-new-co: Ven. Bede: the vine represents the Synagogue; Christ declares it no longer acceptable 'since the figures were not to pass into reality' — the New Covenant.
linkNotes.the-virgin-of-emmanuel-isaiah-7-14|mary: St. Jerome (on 'almah' = virgin) and the Fathers 'generally apply all to Christ'; the virgin sign is fulfilled in Mary.
linkNotes.the-voice-of-the-lord-thunder|baptism: 'The first voice was heard when Jesus was baptized' (Matt 3:17) — the first of the seven voices read of baptism.
linkNotes.the-voice-of-the-lord-thunder|christ: Worthington/Calmet: 'something posterior to the reign of David is prefigured'; the Fathers understood the psalm of the propagation of the gospel and 'our Saviour preaching with great power and majesty.'
linkNotes.the-voice-of-the-lord-thunder|new-covena: 'the rest may intimate the instruction and efficacy of the other sacraments' — the sevenfold voice read of the sacramental system.
linkNotes.the-wilderness-pilgrimage-toward-the-pro: 'we have quitted Egypt by our baptism'; 'All that happened to this chosen people... was a figure of what was to happen to us' (1 Cor 10).
linkNotes.the-year-of-jubilee|christ: Calmet: the year of Jubilee, 'when the Jews should be delivered, as a figure of Christ's redemption.'
linkNotes.water-from-rock|christ: The rock itself is a type of Christ (cf. 1 Cor 10:4)
linkNotes.water-from-rock|spiritual-gifts-of-chris: Water from the rock was the figure of the spiritual gifts of Christ
linkNotes.zechariahs-thirty-pieces-of-silver|the-b: Witham: 'Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by [the prophet]'; the silver cast into the temple and the potter's field bought — Judas's betrayal.
linkNotes.zedekiah|christs-passion: Eusebius/Calmet: 'Thou hast been angry with thy Christ (king Sedecias), and even with our Redeemer, in some sense, as He was treated thus.'
linkNotes.zorobabel|christ: Calmet: 'Zorobabel was only a figure of Him, and never really possessed the throne, that the Jews might not think that the prophecies were fulfilled in his person.'
linkNotes.zorobabel|the-one-true-church: Calmet: 'Zorobabel shall build the temple, as a figure of Christ establishing his Church.'

ccc.117: The spiritual sense. Thanks to the unity of God's plan, not only the text of Scripture but also the realities and events about which it speaks can be signs. (1101) The allegorical sense.
ccc.128: The Church, as early as apostolic times, and then constantly in her Tradition, has illuminated the unity of the divine plan in the two Testaments through typology, which discerns in God's works of the Old Covenant prefigurations of what he accomplished in the fullness of time in the person of his incarnate Son.
ccc.129: Christians therefore read the Old Testament in the light of Christ crucified and risen. Such typological reading discloses the inexhaustible content of the Old Testament; but it must not make us forget that the Old Testament retains its own intrinsic value as Revelation reaffirmed by our Lord himself.
ccc.130: Typology indicates the dynamic movement toward the fulfillment of the divine plan when "God [will] be everything to everyone." Nor do the calling of the patriarchs and the exodus from Egypt, for example, lose their own value in God's plan, from the mere fact that they were intermediate stages.
ccc.489: Throughout the Old Covenant the mission of many holy women prepared for that of Mary. At the very beginning there was Eve; despite her disobedience, she receives the promise of a posterity that will be victorious over the evil one, as well as the promise that she will be the mother of all the living.
ccc.527: Jesus' circumcision, on the eighth day after his birth, is the sign of his incorporation into Abraham's descendants, into the people of the covenant. It is the sign of his submission to the Law and his deputation to Israel's worship, in which he will participate throughout his life.
ccc.1094: It is on this harmony of the two Testaments that the Paschal catechesis of the Lord is built, and then, that of the Apostles and the Fathers of the Church. This catechesis unveils what lay hidden under the letter of the Old Testament: the mystery of Christ.
ccc.1150: Signs of the covenant. The Chosen People received from God distinctive signs and symbols that marked its liturgical life. These are no longer solely celebrations of cosmic cycles and social gestures, but signs of the covenant, symbols of God's mighty deeds for his people.
ccc.1221: But above all, the crossing of the Red Sea, literally the liberation of Israel from the slavery of Egypt, announces the liberation wrought by Baptism: > You freed the children of Abraham from the slavery of Pharaoh, bringing them dry-shod through the waters of the Red Sea, to be an image of the people set free in Bapt…
ccc.1222: Finally, Baptism is prefigured in the crossing of the Jordan River by which the People of God received the gift of the land promised to Abraham's descendants, an image of eternal life. The promise of this blessed inheritance is fulfilled in the New Covenant.
ccc.1334: In the Old Covenant bread and wine were offered in sacrifice among the first fruits of the earth as a sign of grateful acknowledgment to the Creator.
ccc.1544: Everything that the priesthood of the Old Covenant prefigured finds its fulfillment in Christ Jesus, the "one mediator between God and men." The Christian tradition considers Melchizedek, "priest of God Most High," as a prefiguration of the priesthood of Christ, the unique "high priest after the order of Melchizedek";…
ccc.2676: This twofold movement of prayer to Mary has found a privileged expression in the Ave Maria: (722, 490, 435, 146) Hail Mary [or Rejoice, Mary]: the greeting of the angel Gabriel opens this prayer. It is God himself who, through his angel as intermediary, greets Mary.

contextNotes.text: “Reprobate” is an old theological word for those who are finally lost. The Church teaches that no one is rejected in advance: “God predestines no one to go to hell; for this, a willful turning away from God (a mortal sin) is necessary, and persistence in it until the end.”

contextNotes.text: Strictly speaking, Isaiah 7:14 is a prophecy rather than a type: a promise spoken in words, not a person or event that foreshadows. The Catechism treats it as a promise kept: of Jesus' virginal conception it says, “The Church sees here the fulfillment of the divine promise given through the prophet Isaiah.”

ccc.quote: The Church sees here the fulfillment of the divine promise given through the prophet Isaiah
